plants.name: Elkhorn fern

soil.note: Mounted on a board or tree

plants.feedingNote: Dilute liquid fertiliser monthly in the warm months.

pruning.rule: Leave the brown shield fronds at the base; they protect the roots. Remove only dead hanging fronds.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Liquid feed
tasks.description: Apply dilute liquid fertiliser to the fronds and shield, monthly through the warm months.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Staghorn fern

soil.note: Mounted on a board or tree

plants.feedingNote: Organic matter tucked behind the upper shield fronds, or dilute liquid fertiliser, in the warm months.

pruning.rule: Leave the shield fronds; they are meant to brown off. Remove only dead hanging fronds.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Feed with organic matter
tasks.description: Tuck leaf litter, compost or banana peel behind the upper shield fronds, or apply dilute liquid fertiliser.
tasks.howMuch: A handful of organic matter, or half-strength liquid feed

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Soft tree fern
plants.feedingNote: Rarely needed; a layer of leaf litter or compost around the base in spring.

pruning.rule: Cut off only dead, hanging fronds. Never cut the crown.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Water trunk and crown
tasks.description: Wet the full length of the trunk and the crown in dry weather. Check the watering system reaches the trunk, not just the ground.
tasks.criticalReason: The trunk is the root system; if it dries out in summer the fern can die.
tasks.ifMissed: Fronds brown off; a dried-out trunk can kill the fern.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Bird of paradise
plants.feedingNote: Controlled-release or organic fertiliser in spring.

pruning.rule: Remove spent flower stems and dead leaves at the base.

deadhead.note: Spent flower stems rot and look untidy; cut them at the base.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Remove spent flowers and dead leaves
tasks.description: Cut spent flower stems and dead leaves off at the base. Can also be done whenever spent flowers are seen.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Spring feed
tasks.description: Scatter controlled-release or organic fertiliser around the clump and water in.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Giant bird of paradise
plants.feedingNote: Controlled-release fertiliser in spring.

pruning.rule: Remove dead or badly torn leaves at the base; cut off spent flowers.

deadhead.note: Tidier; spent flowers rot in the leaf bases.

plants.cautions: Wind shreds the leaves (cosmetic). Frost-tender.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Remove torn and dead leaves
tasks.description: Cut dead or badly wind-torn leaves off at the base; remove spent flowers.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Waratah
plants.botanicalName: Telopea (species or hybrid to be confirmed)

soil.note: Sandy, very well drained; struggles in poorly drained clay

plants.feedingNote: Rarely needed. If feeding, low-phosphorus controlled-release native fertiliser in early spring. Over-feeding is a common cause of failure.

pruning.rule: After flowering, cut flower stems back by half to three-quarters. Plants about 10 years old can be cut back to the swollen base (lignotuber) after flowering, half one year and half the next. Do not prune newly planted waratahs.

plants.cautions: Needs shelter from wind while flowering to avoid bract burn.

sources: https://www.gardenclinic.com.au/how-to-grow-article/waratah

tasks.title: Prune after flowering
tasks.description: Cut flower stems back by half to three-quarters. On plants about 10 years old, canes can instead be cut back to the swollen base, half the plant one year and half the next. Do not prune newly planted waratahs.
tasks.howMuch: Half to three-quarters of each flower stem
tasks.ifMissed: Fewer, leggier flowering stems next year.

sources: https://www.gardenclinic.com.au/how-to-grow-article/waratah

tasks.title: Native fertiliser (only if needed)
tasks.description: Only if growth is poor: apply low-phosphorus controlled-release native fertiliser in early spring. Waratahs rarely need feeding.
tasks.ifMissed: Usually nothing; over-feeding does more harm.

sources: https://www.gardenclinic.com.au/how-to-grow-article/waratah

plants.name: Protea
plants.botanicalName: Protea spp. (several types; to be listed)
plants.feedingNote: Usually none. If needed, low-phosphorus native fertiliser.

pruning.rule: Cut flowered stems back into the leafy part of the stem. Never cut into bare wood; it rarely reshoots.

plants.cautions: Phosphorus-sensitive: no general-purpose fertiliser or rich compost nearby.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Prune after flowering
tasks.description: Cut flowered stems back into the leafy part of the stem. Never cut into bare wood.
tasks.ifMissed: Plant becomes leggy and flowers less.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Native hibiscus
plants.feedingNote: Light feed of native fertiliser in spring.

pruning.rule: Prune by up to about a third immediately after the main spring flowering.

plants.cautions: Often short-lived (several years).

sources: https://www.burkesbackyard.com.au/blogs/expert-answers/dons-expert-answers-when-and-how-do-you-prune-a-native-hibiscus/

tasks.title: Prune after spring flowering
tasks.description: Tip prune or cut back immediately after the main spring flowering to keep the plant dense.

sources: https://www.burkesbackyard.com.au/blogs/expert-answers/dons-expert-answers-when-and-how-do-you-prune-a-native-hibiscus/

plants.name: Lavender
plants.feedingNote: Rarely needed.

pruning.rule: Cut back by about a third, staying within the leafy growth. Bare old wood rarely reshoots.

deadhead.note: Trimming spent flower spikes keeps plants compact.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Prune after flowering
tasks.description: Cut back by about a third, staying within the leafy growth. Do not cut into bare old wood.
tasks.ifMissed: Plants become woody and open in the centre.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Pelargonium
plants.feedingNote: Light feed in spring.

pruning.rule: Cut back by a half to two-thirds, just above a leaf node; reshoots readily.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Deadhead
tasks.description: Snap or cut off spent flower heads.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Rejuvenation prune
tasks.description: Cut back to just above a leaf node.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Hydrangea
plants.feedingNote: Compost or general fertiliser in spring. Acid soil gives blue flowers, alkaline soil pink.

pruning.rule: Cut stems that flowered back to the first pair of fat buds. Leave stems that did not flower; they carry next year's flowers.

deadhead.note: Old heads can stay over winter and are removed at winter pruning.

plants.cautions: Not irrigated: mulch in late spring to hold moisture between visits.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Winter prune
tasks.description: Cut stems that flowered back to the first pair of fat buds. Leave stems that did not flower this year.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Deep water and mulch
tasks.description: Water deeply during visits in dry weather. Mulch in late spring to hold moisture between visits.
tasks.howMuch: A full bucket per plant per watering
tasks.ifMissed: Wilting and leaf scorch; usually recovers after rain.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Daffodil
plants.feedingNote: None needed; leaves left to die back feed the bulb.

pruning.rule: Do not cut or tie green leaves. Remove them only once fully yellow.

deadhead.note: Removing spent flowers stops seed-setting and sends energy to the bulb.

plants.cautions: Bulbs are poisonous.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Plant new bulbs (only if adding)
tasks.description: Plant bulbs pointed end up, about twice as deep as the bulb is tall. Existing bulbs return each year and need no replanting.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Remove spent foliage
tasks.description: Once leaves are fully yellow (about six weeks after flowering), cut them off at ground level. Do not cut or tie green leaves.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Arum lily

soil.note: Moist or boggy; also tolerates drier soil

plants.feedingNote: None needed.

pruning.rule: Remove yellow leaves and spent flower stems at the base.

deadhead.note: Removing flower heads before seeds form stops birds spreading it.

plants.cautions: Environmental weed in coastal southern Victoria (declared in SA and WA, not in Victoria). Birds spread the seed. All parts poisonous.

sources: https://weeds.org.au/profiles/arum-lily-calla/

tasks.title: Tidy foliage
tasks.description: Remove yellowing leaves and spent flower stems at the base.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Remove flower heads before seeding
tasks.description: Cut off flower heads as they fade, before the green seed heads form. Birds spread the seed into bushland.
tasks.ifMissed: Seedlings spread into nearby bushland and creek lines.

sources: https://weeds.org.au/profiles/arum-lily-calla/

plants.name: Canna lily
plants.feedingNote: Compost or general fertiliser in spring.

pruning.rule: Cut stems to ground level once they die back in winter.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Cut back
tasks.description: Cut stems to the ground once the foliage has died back.
tasks.ifMissed: Untidy; old stems can harbour pests.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Passionfruit
plants.feedingNote: Citrus or fruit fertiliser (higher potassium) in spring and again in late summer.

pruning.rule: Thin crowded, tangled growth by up to a third in spring. Avoid heavy cuts into old wood. Remove any shoots from below the graft.

harvest.signs: Ripe when the fruit falls, or the skin is fully coloured and starting to wrinkle. Collect fallen fruit every visit.
harvest.storage: About one week at room temperature; up to about two to three weeks in the fridge. Freeze the pulp for longer.

plants.cautions: Frost-tender. On grafted vines, rootstock suckers can take over.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Feed (higher potassium)
tasks.description: Apply citrus or fruit fertiliser around the root zone (not against the stem) and water in. Spring and late summer.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Thin growth
tasks.description: Thin out crowded and tangled growth to let in air and light. Avoid heavy cuts into old wood.
tasks.ifMissed: Tangled vine; more disease, smaller crop.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Remove rootstock suckers
tasks.description: Look for shoots coming from below the graft (the bump near the base) or from the roots. Cut or pull them off where they start.
tasks.criticalReason: On grafted vines, suckers from the rootstock grow fast and can replace the fruiting variety.
tasks.ifMissed: The rootstock takes over; the vine may stop producing good fruit.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Bougainvillea
plants.feedingNote: Light feed in spring; too much nitrogen gives leaves instead of flowers.

pruning.rule: Can be cut back hard after flowering to control size; flowers form on new growth.

plants.cautions: Thorny. Frost-tender; marginal in cool coastal Victoria.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Prune after flowering
tasks.description: Cut back to control size and shape; flowers form on new growth.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Bird's nest fern
plants.feedingNote: Dilute liquid fertiliser in the warm months.

pruning.rule: Remove only dead or damaged outer fronds.

plants.cautions: Frost-tender. Not on the watering system.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Root watering
tasks.description: Keep the root ball moist; do not water into the central nest (it can rot).

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Yucca
plants.feedingNote: Rarely needed.

pruning.rule: Remove dead lower leaves and spent flower spikes. Stems can be cut back to reduce height; they reshoot.

plants.cautions: Sharp leaf tips.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Remove dead leaves
tasks.description: Pull or cut off dead lower leaves; remove spent flower spikes.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Sunflower
plants.feedingNote: Compost dug in before sowing.

pruning.rule: Annual; no pruning. Thin seedlings to their final spacing early.

deadhead.note: Leave heads to ripen seed, for harvest or birds.

harvest.signs: Seed is ready when the back of the head turns yellow-brown and the petals have dropped. Cover heads with a paper bag or net to keep birds off.
harvest.storage: Dried seed keeps for months in an airtight jar.

plants.cautions: Tall plants may need staking in wind.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Sow seeds
tasks.description: Sow directly into the bed once the soil has warmed. Sowing at the start of the summer holidays allows watering while seedlings establish.
tasks.howMuch: 2–3 seeds per spot; spots at final spacing

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Thin seedlings
tasks.description: When seedlings have two true leaves, keep the strongest at each spot and snip the rest at soil level (pulling disturbs roots).
tasks.ifMissed: Crowded, weak plants with small heads.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Deep watering
tasks.description: Water deeply during visits as flower heads form; mulch to hold moisture.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Kangaroo paw
plants.feedingNote: Light feed of native fertiliser in spring.

pruning.rule: Cut flowered stems and old leaves down to the base after flowering.

plants.cautions: Prone to ink disease (black leaf marks) in humid conditions; remove affected leaves.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Cut back after flowering
tasks.description: Cut flowered stems and old leaves right down to the base.
tasks.ifMissed: Untidy plant, fewer flowers, more ink disease.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Birch
plants.feedingNote: Rarely needed; mulch the root zone.

pruning.rule: Avoid pruning if possible. Remove only dead, damaged or crossing branches, between late summer and mid-winter. From late winter the sap rises and cuts bleed heavily.

plants.cautions: Shallow roots compete with nearby plants. Suffers in long dry spells.

sources: https://www.rhs.org.uk/pruning/bleeding-from-cuts
Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Remove dead or crossing branches (only if needed)
tasks.description: Remove only dead, damaged or crossing branches. Do not prune from late winter to spring; cuts bleed sap heavily.
tasks.ifMissed: Nothing, if the tree is healthy.

sources: https://www.rhs.org.uk/pruning/bleeding-from-cuts

tasks.title: Deep water in dry spells
tasks.description: Water deeply during visits in dry weather, especially young trees. Mulch the root zone.
tasks.ifMissed: Leaf drop and dieback in long dry spells.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Grapevine
plants.botanicalName: Vitis vinifera (table grape; variety to be confirmed)
plants.feedingNote: Light feed of compost or complete fertiliser in spring; too much nitrogen gives leaves instead of fruit.

pruning.rule: Winter: remove up to about 90% of last season's growth. Spur pruning cuts each cane back to two buds.

harvest.signs: Ripe when bunches are fully coloured, the berries taste sweet and the seeds are brown. Grapes do not ripen further once picked.
harvest.storage: About one to two weeks in the fridge, unwashed.

plants.cautions: Birds take ripening fruit: net from when berries start to colour. Mildew risk in humid coastal weather; keep the canopy open.

sources: https://sybilsfruits.blogspot.com/2020/01/how-to-prune-grapevines-in-australia.html
Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Winter prune
tasks.description: Spur pruning: cut each of last season's canes back to a spur of two buds. Cut a few millimetres above a bud.
tasks.criticalReason: Grapes fruit on new shoots from last year's wood; without winter pruning the vine tangles and crops poorly for the season.
tasks.howMuch: Up to about 90% of last season's growth
tasks.ifMissed: A season's crop is reduced, and the vine becomes harder to manage.

sources: https://sybilsfruits.blogspot.com/2020/01/how-to-prune-grapevines-in-australia.html

tasks.title: Summer trim and thin
tasks.description: Shorten long shoots a few leaves past the last bunch; remove some leaves around bunches to let in air and light.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Spring feed
tasks.description: Spread compost or a light application of complete fertiliser around the root zone.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Agave
plants.feedingNote: Not needed.

pruning.rule: Remove only dead or damaged leaves at the base; cut green leaves scar permanently.

plants.cautions: Flowers once and then dies; offsets (pups) replace it. Mild frosts only. Spineless.

sources: https://www.nurseriesonline.com.au/plant-index/succulents/agave-attenuata/

tasks.title: Remove dead leaves and unwanted pups
tasks.description: Cut off dead lower leaves at the base. Remove offsets (pups) if the clump is spreading too far; they can be replanted.

sources: https://www.nurseriesonline.com.au/plant-index/succulents/agave-attenuata/

plants.name: Baby's tears
plants.feedingNote: Not needed.

pruning.rule: Trim freely to contain; regrows quickly.

plants.cautions: Frost-sensitive; may die back in cold winters. Spreads readily into lawns and paths.

sources: https://www.burkesbackyard.com.au/fact-sheets/in-the-garden/grasses-ground-covers-lawns/babys-tears/
Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Water in dry spells
tasks.description: Water during visits in dry weather. It may brown off between visits and usually regrows.

sources: https://www.burkesbackyard.com.au/fact-sheets/in-the-garden/grasses-ground-covers-lawns/babys-tears/

tasks.title: Trim edges
tasks.description: Trim the edges to stop it spreading into lawns and paths.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Aloe
plants.feedingNote: Not needed.

pruning.rule: Remove spent flower stalks and dead lower leaves.

deadhead.note: Cut spent flower stalks at the base.

plants.cautions: Can spread into bushland in some coastal areas.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

tasks.title: Remove spent flower stalks
tasks.description: Cut spent flower stalks at the base after winter flowering; remove dead lower leaves.

sources: Claude: general horticultural knowledge (not yet checked against a published source)

plants.name: Cycad
plants.feedingNote: Controlled-release fertiliser in spring; in coastal or alkaline soil add trace elements (iron, manganese, zinc).

pruning.rule: Remove only brown or fully yellow fronds, close to the trunk; green fronds feed the plant.

plants.cautions: All parts poisonous, especially the seeds; keep away from pets and children. Sharp leaf tips.

sources: https://www.bunnings.com.au/diy-advice/garden/planting-and-growing/how-to-grow-and-care-for-a-cycad

tasks.title: Remove dead fronds
tasks.description: Cut brown or fully yellow fronds off close to the trunk with secateurs or long-handled loppers. Leave green fronds.

sources: https://www.bunnings.com.au/diy-advice/garden/planting-and-growing/how-to-grow-and-care-for-a-cycad

tasks.title: Spring feed
tasks.description: Apply controlled-release fertiliser for trees and shrubs. In coastal or alkaline soil, add trace elements (iron, manganese, zinc).

sources: https://www.bunnings.com.au/diy-advice/garden/planting-and-growing/how-to-grow-and-care-for-a-cycad

plants.name: Cabbage tree (red)

sun.note: Full sun to light shade; light shade keeps red leaf colour richer

plants.feedingNote: Light feed in spring if growth is slow.

pruning.rule: Remove old lower leaves as they die. In spring, cut out winter-damaged growth just above a side shoot or at a sound point on the trunk. An overgrown plant can be cut through the main stem in mid-spring; it resprouts.

deadhead.note: Faded flower spikes can be removed, or left to produce berries.

plants.cautions: Coloured-leaf forms are less hardy than green ones. Tying the leaves together reduces wind damage. Tough leaf fibres can jam mowers and are slow to compost.

sources: https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/popular/cordyline/growing-guide

tasks.title: Remove dead lower leaves
tasks.description: Pull or cut off dead and dying lower leaves. Cut out any winter-damaged growth just above a side shoot or at a sound point on the trunk.

sources: https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/popular/cordyline/growing-guide

tasks.title: Remove faded flower spikes (optional)
tasks.description: Cut faded flower spikes off at their base, or leave them for the berries.

sources: https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/popular/cordyline/growing-guide
